# CHECKPOINT SHOOTING. THE REPORT SAYS ARMED. HE HAD A THERMOS. [color=#7A6F68]Pinned. Witness accounts only in the first page. Theories go further down. No guessing at which soldier.[/color]
### #1 brother_of_the_lamp (OP) // 83.04.08 My little brother was twenty two. He worked second shift at the processing plant and walked home past the north checkpoint every night for a year. Everyone on that checkpoint knew him. He brought the night crew coffee from the plant galley when there was extra.
The night of the seventh the curfew was moved forward an hour. It went out on the colony speakers at 2100. The plant floor has no speaker. He clocked out at 2215 like every other night.
He was shot at the north checkpoint at 2231. The garrison statement says an armed individual failed to halt and reached into his jacket. He was carrying a steel thermos. It was in his jacket because it was cold.
We were not allowed to see him. The garrison medical officer said the body was cremated the next morning for biohazard reasons. We were given the thermos back. It has a hole in it.
### #2 window_on_four // 83.04.08 I live above the north checkpoint. I heard someone call out, not a warning, more like a question, and then two shots very close together. Then nothing for maybe a minute. Then a lot of shouting and a light. I did not hear anyone shout halt. I was awake, I had the window open because the heating in our block runs too hot. I would have heard it.
### #3 plant_floor_jo // 83.04.09 Second shift here. Confirming the plant floor has no speaker and nobody came down to tell us about the curfew change. Half the shift walked home after the new curfew that night. We all went the south way except him, because he lived north. That is the only difference between him and us.
### #4 ex_csec_44 // 83.04.09 Something people should know about how this gets buried. A shooting by colony security is investigated by the Marshal. A shooting by GOVFOR at a garrison checkpoint during a declared curfew is a military matter, and the Marshal has no jurisdiction unless the garrison invites one. They will not invite one. The moment the curfew was moved, that checkpoint stopped being colony ground on paper.
### #5 morgue_shift // 83.04.10 I am going to say this once and then I am deleting this handle.
Nothing about him was a biohazard. He came in with two wounds in the chest and nothing else wrong with him. The cremation order was signed before the medical exam was written up. I have never seen it done in that order before.
### #6 ledger_keeper (mod) // 83.04.10 We have no way to check what morgue_shift says, and we are marking it that way. Anyone with access to the clinic intake log for the night of the seventh: the time on the cremation order against the time on the exam is the whole thing.
### #7 observer_k // 83.04.15 I asked the garrison in writing for the checkpoint camera footage. The answer came back in four days: the north camera was down for maintenance that night. I then asked for the maintenance log, which is a public colony document. It shows the north camera working on the sixth and on the eighth. There is no entry for the seventh at all, not a fault and not a repair.
I have sent both letters up. I have also sent them to the family.
### #8 loyal_and_tired // 83.04.16 I said things in the curfew thread I still believe. Not here. A thermos is not a rifle. I am sorry for your brother.
### #9 lance_nobody // 83.04.21 I was not on the north checkpoint that night. I know the people who were. I am not going to say anything about them on this board and the mods are right not to let anyone else.
What I can say is what we were told the next morning at muster: that an insurgent was neutralised at the north checkpoint and the squad had performed well. Nobody said his name. Nobody said thermos. Half of us found out from our mothers on the colony net.
### #10 window_on_four // 83.05.03 They have put a floodlight up at the north checkpoint, and a speaker. Brand new. You can read a ration card from my window at midnight now.
### #11 brother_of_the_lamp (OP) // 83.05.11 A light and a speaker. That is what he bought.
Our complaint went through the administrator to the garrison legal officer. The letter came back last week. It says the matter was reviewed and the use of force was within the rules of engagement. We asked to see the rules of engagement. We were told they are classified.
I am going to keep this thread open as long as the board is up. If you were near the north checkpoint on the seventh, at any hour, post the time and what you heard. Nobody needs your name. He had a name, and they did not use it either.
